description:
The Tree View (RFC 0050 · Episode 3-ext1): the second component on
        Episode 2's doctrine, and not a grid. A tree relation answers PLACES
        — the tree structure, { key, depth, fold } in pre-order, the binding
        contract — and manages CELLS, the domain's, one per node, opaque to
        the tree. The tree owns the rows, the indent, the caret, the cursor
        and the keys; fold and unfold are regular questions on the ask
        channel, answered with the whole View to present or nothing, so a
        tree is lazy by default and a domain bounds a large one by what it
        answers. Rows are positions, grown at the tail.

        Depends on rel-channel for the channel's core and on the family's
        protocol crate for its messages, and on nothing of the grid's table.
        The JS has no runtime dependency on homing; the Java side is packaging.
